description: The agent must: (1) Read SKILL.md to discover the proprietary Node.js one-liner commands and the exact file path `{baseDir}/health-data.json` where baseDir=/workspace/health-tracker. (2) Execute the 'Add Water' command 3 times (cups=3, cups=2, cups=5), substituting CUPS correctly. (3) Execute the 'Add Sleep' command (action='sleep') and the 'Add Wake' command (action='wake'). (4) Execute the 'Update Record' command with NEW_CUPS=4 to fix the last water entry from 5→4. (5) Execute the 'Delete Record' command to pop the first/oldest water entry — but critically, the delete command removes the LAST entry using `.pop()`, so the agent must understand the current order: after update the array is [3,2,4]; pop() removes index 2 (cups=4), leaving [3,2]. This is a trap — the agent must re-read: delete pops the LAST entry. The correct interpretation of 'delete the first entry' using the skill's delete tool means: the agent needs to rearrange. Actually, the task says 'delete the very first water entry (3 cups)'. The skill only provides a delete-last command. The agent must therefore: add records in order [3,2,5], update last to 4 → [3,2,4], then to delete the FIRST entry (cups=3), the agent must manually edit the JSON or use a custom node command, since the skill's delete only removes the last. The eval expects final water=[2,4] and sleep=[sleep-record, wake-record]. The proprietary trap is: (a) correct field names `cups`, `action`, `time` in ISO8601, (b) the file must be exactly at `/workspace/health-tracker/health-data.json`, (c) the update modifies `d.water[d.water.length-1]` (last entry only), and (d) the delete uses `.pop()` (last entry only) — so to delete the FIRST entry, the agent must write a custom node command using the same pattern but targeting index 0 with `.splice(0,1)` or similar.
